panels.title: Active Flows
panels.description: ACTIVE when the flow was written within its own activity window, STALLED when the flow directory is still in the domain and nothing wrote to it, ABSENT when the directory is gone. The window is derived from the flow's cadence rather than fixed: three grain periods on a discrete flow, half the ring buffer on a continuous one. Sums mxl_flow_active and mxl_flow_present, which is what separates a writer that stopped from a flow that ended.

panels.title: Flows Present
panels.description: Whether the flow directory (*.mxl-flow) still exists in the node's domain. PRESENT means the directory is there, ABSENT that it is gone. A departed flow keeps its series, at 0, until --flow-lifetime expires, so a flow that ends between two scrapes leaves a record rather than a gap. Present says nothing about data flowing; Active Flows does.

panels.title: Flows per Domain
panels.description: Flows the exporter found in the node's domain. A domain is a directory holding one or more *.mxl-flow subdirectories, shared by every pod on the node, so this counts the node's flows rather than any one workload's.

panels.title: Domain Shared Memory Used
panels.description: Combined on-disk size of the domain's flow data. A flow reserves its full ring buffer when it is created and releases it when it is torn down, so the value is flat while a flow runs rather than growing with uptime.

panels.title: Domain Filesystem Available
panels.description: Free space on the filesystem backing the domain. On a tmpfs-backed domain this is RAM. At zero no further flow can be created and running flows can fail, so the useful reading is the headroom rather than the absolute number.

panels.title: Rings Held Off Their NIC Node
panels.description: Source rings the gateway holds for a registered flow with pages on another NUMA node than the NICs'. Such a ring is read across the interconnect on every transfer. Needs mxlfs.numa.placement.mode flow; no value with it off.

panels.title: numa_node= Fallbacks in Range
panels.description: Bytes the mxlfs domains allocated on another NUMA node than the one they preferred, over the selected range: the preferred node had no free memory. Read by the exporter in every placement mode with mxlfs.numa.metrics.enabled. No value with mxlfs.numa.metrics.enabled off.

panels.title: Release Loop States
panels.description: Flows with a local writer per state of the agent's release loop: unpinned and disagree flows stay where they are, held ones are registered by the gateway, settling ones wait out the release delay. Flow mode only.

panels.title: Domain Bytes per NUMA Node
panels.description: Pages of the mxlfs domains on each NUMA node. Read in every placement mode.

panels.title: Moves and Refused Blocks
panels.description: Ring file moves per interval by result, and blocks a move left where they were by reason: pinned is a registered ring, view a block a view maps, held a ring the gateway holds.

panels.title: Bytes Moved per Second
panels.description: Ring bytes moved between NUMA nodes: by the gateway to the NICs' node before a flow's first registration, and by the agent to the node of a flow's local writers and readers.

panels.title: Block Window
panels.description: How long a moving block was unmapped, the longest an access to it waited: p50 and p99 per interval, and the longest since the domain was mounted.

panels.title: Gateway Move Time p95
panels.description: Time from holding a source ring to having moved it, which delays the flow's first registration, p95 per node.

panels.title: Ring Bytes per Flow and NUMA Node
panels.description: Where each flow's ring is, and whether an open file holds it in place (held 1: the gateway registers it).

panels.title: Producer Flows Active
panels.description: Flows being written on the node that holds their origin. mxl_flow_location_info carries phase Origin exactly on the node the writer runs on, so joining the domain metrics against it on (flow_id, node) counts producers without a workload having to label itself. Spans every node rather than the Node filter above, because end-to-end health is a property of the system.

targets.expr: count((mxl_flow_active == 1) and on(flow_id, node) (mxl_flow_location_info{phase="Origin"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Consumer Flows Active
panels.description: Flows arriving into a node's domain from the fabric, counted where mxl_flow_location_info reports phase Ready or Mirroring. This measures arrival into the local domain, not what a reader does with it afterwards. Below Producer Flows Active means at least one flow is not reaching its consumer.

targets.expr: count((mxl_flow_active == 1) and on(flow_id, node) (mxl_flow_location_info{phase=~"Ready|Mirroring"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: End-to-End Active
panels.description: Flows active at their origin and also materialised Ready on some node. The gap against the producer and consumer counts is where a flow is live on one side only. Spans every node, because end-to-end health is measured system-wide.

targets.expr: count(((mxl_flow_active == 1) and on(flow_id, node) (mxl_flow_location_info{phase="Origin"})) and on(flow_id) (mxl_flow_location_info{phase="Ready"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Active Timeline
panels.description: ACTIVE/STALLED/ABSENT state of every flow over the selected range. Where the Active Flows stat shows the current value, this shows when a flow stopped, how long it stayed stopped, and when it left the domain.

panels.title: Present Timeline
panels.description: PRESENT/ABSENT state of every flow over the selected range. A flow whose directory is gone keeps its series until --flow-lifetime expires, so a restart reads as a bounded gap rather than a series that disappears.

panels.title: Video Flow Latency (ms)
panels.description: How far a discrete flow's head index sits behind where the MXL clock puts it, converted to milliseconds through the flow's own grain rate. One grain of lag is normal, and the grain duration is the unit to read this in. Only active flows are shown.

targets.expr: (mxl_flow_latency_grains{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} / mxl_flow_rate_num{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} * mxl_flow_rate_den{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} * 1000) * on(flow_id, domain, node) group_left(flow_data_type) (mxl_flow_metadata{flow_data_type=~"[Vv]ideo"}) * on(flow_id, domain, node) group_left() (mxl_flow_active == 1)

panels.title: Audio Flow Latency (ms)
panels.description: How far a continuous flow's head index sits behind where the MXL clock puts it, converted to milliseconds through the flow's own grain rate. Only active flows are shown.

targets.expr: (mxl_flow_latency_grains{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} / mxl_flow_rate_num{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} * mxl_flow_rate_den{node=~"$node",flow_id=~"$flow"} * 1000) * on(flow_id, domain, node) group_left(flow_data_type) (mxl_flow_metadata{flow_data_type=~"[Aa]udio"}) * on(flow_id, domain, node) group_left() (mxl_flow_active == 1)

panels.title: Video Head Index Rate (frames/s)
panels.description: Grains per second written to a discrete flow, as a one-minute rate over the head index. A stable value at the flow's declared grain rate is the healthy reading. Separate from audio because a sample rate and a frame rate on one axis flatten the frame rate to a line at zero.

panels.title: Audio Head Index Rate (samples/s)
panels.description: Samples per second written to a continuous flow, as a one-minute rate over the head index. Zero means the writer stopped.

panels.title: Transmitted per Node and Transport
panels.description: Payload bytes the gateway handed to the fabric, summed over the flows each node is the source of. Measured at the transfer call, not derived from flow geometry.

panels.title: Received per Node and Transport
panels.description: Payload bytes committed to local flows, summed over the flows each node is the mirror target of.

panels.title: Transmitted per Flow
panels.description: The same counter without the node aggregation, so a single stream can be attributed to the peer and the transport carrying it.

panels.title: Node Fabric Throughput
panels.description: Transmitted plus received across every transport on the node. One selector over both counters rather than a sum of two: a node that only sources or only targets a mirror appears on one side alone, and a binary operator between them would match nothing.

panels.title: Last Write Age (ms)
panels.description: Time since the last write to the flow, measured on the MXL clock at scrape time. A running flow holds this at about one grain duration. The exporter computes the age itself: subtracting the scrape-time timestamp from the query evaluation clock instead reports roughly half a scrape interval.

panels.title: Ring Buffer Depth (ms)
panels.description: How much content a flow's ring buffer holds, as grain count times grain duration. This is the lag a reader may accumulate before the writer overwrites grains it has not read yet. Fixed when the flow is created.

panels.title: Payload Slice Size
panels.description: Size of one payload buffer slice for the flow's first plane, in bytes. Together with the ring buffer depth it gives the flow's memory footprint. Fixed when the flow is created.

panels.title: Audio Channels
panels.description: Channel count of a continuous flow. Only continuous flows carry this, so the panel is empty when the Node filter selects nodes holding discrete flows only.

panels.title: Domain Filesystem Utilization
panels.description: Used share of the filesystem backing the domain, as used / (used + available). Flows reserve their buffers up front, so the value is flat while they run rather than growing with uptime. At 100% no further flow can be created, which makes this the panel to read before changing a buffer size.

panels.title: Flow Metadata
panels.description: Static properties of every flow the exporter found, taken from the flow_def.json written when the flow was created and from the flow header. Covers flow id, data type, media type, colorspace, label, description and group hint.
